title: preflight-stream-probes-and-mime-fallbacks-for-tool-attachments
author: Priya Raman
body:
Context and motivation: We've seen multiple customer reports and fuzzing runs where malformed multipart payloads or mislabeled Content-Type headers caused the OpenAI-compat layer to accept binary blobs that later triggered model-serving failures or excessive memory copies. This PR introduces a light-weight preflight probing stage for tool/file attachments plus robust MIME fallback detection and additional safety checks to prevent streaming stalls and silent truncation.

Changes and high-level design: Adds an attachment preflight probe (default: first 8 KiB) that is used to: 1) heuristically detect Content-Type using internal sniffers and libmagic as a fallback, 2) compute a rolling SHA256 prefix used for early integrity checks during streaming ingestion, 3) validate that declared Content-Length (if present) matches the Summarized-Length we derive from chunked/form-data metadata. The preflight is non-blocking for small files and performed inline for larger streams with a configurable probe timeout (default 200ms) to avoid hurting latency SLOs.

Compatibility: The OpenAI compatibility layer maps incoming file param names and content-type hints into a normalized Attachment struct used by tool/function calls. To avoid breaking existing clients, we accept the legacy param names (file, files[], input_file) and normalize them. We add a new response error code 4227 (attachment_content_mismatch) when a detected/mapped MIME does not align with the declared mime and user-specified tool schema. Clients will see the new X-Redwood-File-Probe-Length response header when probing occurred.

Security and limits: Introduces hard limits per-attachment and per-request enforced at the compat layer and validated by the runtime: per-attachment soft limit 100MiB (policy warning), hard limit 512MiB (reject), per-request combined attachments 1GiB hard cap. Tool-level override supported for enterprise/private deployments via policy. Unknown/unsafe MIME types are rejected for tool invocations unless explicitly permitted via tool manifest.

Streaming stability improvements: Adds backpressure-aware buffering during preflight and stream commit phases, explicit Content-Length vs chunked consistency checks, and detection of truncated multipart boundaries (returning 400 with clear diagnostics). Also ensures we do not hold entire attachments in memory for tools that accept streaming processing — we wire probe metadata into the stream pipeline so downstream consumers get the probe head and then the rest of the body with minimal copying.

Tests and rollout: Unit tests for libmagic fallback and probe timeout behaviour, integration tests exercising OpenAI-compat parameter name permutations, and an end-to-end canary in perf-canary verifying no measurable latency regression on short text-only requests. Feature is behind a rollout flag (compat.attachment_preflight) and will be enabled for 10% of hosted API traffic after merge, then ramped based on telemetry.

Implementation notes (commits below) and files changed (high level) provide more context.

Risk and mitigation: The main risk is increased tail latency for attachment endpoints; mitigations: probe timeout, probe size tunables, and initial 10% rollout with close SLO monitoring. We also added a failing-fast mode for private installs to keep behaviour deterministic during upgrades.

See related work: ENG-4892 (mime sniffing library integration), ENG-4971 (compat layer file param mapping).
commits: a1f4b2d: add preflight probe abstraction and configuration
c32e7a9: integrate libmagic fallback into mime detector and expose probe header
f5e1d3b: wire probe metadata into streaming ingestion pipeline with backpressure support
d9b8c6e: add unit + integration tests for probe timeouts and legacy param normalization
e0f7a11: update OpenAI compat mapping, add new error code 4227 and documentation
files_changed: rdrd/tests/test_mime_probe.py - unit tests for sniffing and libmagic fallback
perf-canary/jobs/attachment-canary.yaml - canary definition for perf regression
docs/api/attachments.md - docs and new response header X-Redwood-File-Probe-Length
review_comments: Jacob Lee: Good coverage. One question — why 8 KiB as the default probe size? Is this empirically derived?
Priya Raman: Chosen after running attachments corpus: 95% of MIME sniffing decisions stabilized within 6 KiB; 8 KiB gives headroom for multipart headers. Made configurable via probe_size_bytes.
Soraya Khan: Need to ensure we don't regress streaming memory. Please add perf histogram for peak mem during preflight processing.
Priya Raman: Added peak_mem metric and packed the preflight state machine so it can be zero-copy when libmagic not invoked.
Marco Villanueva: Approve after test for deprecated param input_file is added to integration suite.
Priya Raman: Added extra permutations to test_compat_file_params.py and a note in docs about legacy names.
release_notes: Attachment preflight probe and MIME fallback: improves safety and error diagnostics for tool/file uploads; adds new error code 4227 and X-Redwood-File-Probe-Length header. Feature gated rollout.
